title: A Closed Mouth Catches No Flies
subtitle: Opportunities Come to Those Who Speak and Take Action
author: Babi Magil
summary: This proverb teaches that people who never express their needs, ideas, or ambitions may miss opportunities. Success often requires courage, communication, and the willingness to take action.

sections.heading: The Proverb
content: “A closed mouth catches no flies.”

sections.heading: Origin & History
content: This proverb is found across several African and global oral traditions and does not have a confirmed single ethnic owner.
The saying uses a simple image from everyday life: a mouth that remains closed cannot catch anything. Traditionally, elders used such examples to teach people about initiative and communication.

sections.heading: Meaning
content: The proverb teaches that people must speak, ask, and act if they want opportunities.
Someone who remains silent about their goals, needs, or ideas may lose chances that could improve their life.
It does not encourage careless talking, but rather meaningful communication and courage.

sections.heading: Cultural Significance
content: In many African societies, communication has always been important for learning, solving problems, and maintaining relationships.
Elders taught young people that respect and humility should be combined with the courage to speak when necessary.

sections.heading: Story
content: In a village near a busy market, there lived a young woman named Amara who made beautiful woven baskets.
Many people admired her baskets, but Amara kept them hidden because she was afraid that nobody would buy them.
Every market day, she watched other traders sell their products while she sat quietly with her baskets at home.
One day, an elderly trader asked her, 'Why do you hide something that people may value?'
Amara replied, 'I am afraid to speak and offer my work.'
The elder smiled and said, 'A closed mouth cannot receive what the world wants to give.'
The next market day, Amara displayed her baskets and told people about her work.
Many customers admired her skills, and soon she became known throughout the region.
She learned that opportunities often come to those who are brave enough to present themselves.

sections.heading: Life Lessons
content: Speak up when opportunities appear.
Courage creates possibilities.
Ideas have value when they are shared.
Do not allow fear to hide your talents.
Action is necessary for success.

sections.heading: Modern Application
content: This proverb applies to business, careers, education, and relationships. People must communicate their ideas, apply for opportunities, and ask for help when needed.
Talent alone is not enough; people must also be willing to present and use their abilities.
